_comment: Single source for the in-game Guide (BotGuideScreen) and the generated wiki pages in docs/wiki. Placeholders: {bot} = the selected bot's name, {guideKey} = the Guide hotkey. answer: what a fren says when asked how to use this (1 to 3 plain sentences, spoken by the fren, no formatting codes). After editing, run ./gradlew wikiExport and commit docs/wiki.

topics.title: Set up AI companions
topics.summary: Optional: let companions talk back in their own words. Frens works fully without it.
topics.answer: Press the AI setup button at the top right of the Guide and follow the checklist: install Ollama, download a model, turn Soul Chat on, then enable each fren. It all runs on the machine that hosts the world.
details: Everything else in Frens (skills, following, building, scripted lines) works with no AI at all.

AI chat runs a local model through Ollama on the machine that runs the world (the server machine in multiplayer). Chats go only to that Ollama, not to an online service. Downloading a model fetches it from Ollama's registry.
Open the checklist with the AI setup button at the top right of this guide, or Setup… on the Soul Chat row in Bot Controls.
It walks you through: install Ollama, download a model (1B ≈4 GB RAM, 3B ≈6 GB, 8B ≈12 GB, plus Minecraft's own memory), turn Soul Chat on, enable each companion, then say hi in chat.
Soul Chat is the world-wide switch. Each companion also has to be enabled. The checklist shows both.
In multiplayer only an operator or the host can change the server's AI settings. You can still enable your own companions.
Voice is optional and can be added last.
topics.command: UI: Guide > AI setup (or /bot soul system on, /bot soul enable <bot>)
topics.shortcuts: Guide header: AI setup | Bot Controls: Soul Chat > Setup…
topics.tags: ai llm ollama model soul souls chat talk reply persona setup install enable voice optional

topics.title: Talk to Nearby Bots (Group Chat)
topics.summary: Start chat with Bots or All bots instead of naming each companion.
topics.answer: Type in normal chat, without a slash, and start with Bots or All bots, like: Bots, what should we do next? Up to four of your frens within 32 blocks join in, nearest first, when Soul Chat is on.
details: Type in normal chat, without a slash: Bots, what should we do next?
All bots, how is everyone doing? works too.
With Soul Chat on, up to four nearby companions with active Soul profiles join the conversation, nearest first.
They must be within 32 blocks in the same world. Normally only your owned bots qualify. Operators can also address other owners' bots.
If only one companion qualifies, they receive the message directly. A group conversation does not require every bot to reply.
Voice input works the same way if your dictation sends the words into normal Minecraft chat. Frens does not provide microphone transcription itself.
When you are the only player online, everyone, guys, y'all and you two work too.
topics.command: Normal chat: Bots, what should we do next? (no slash)
topics.shortcuts: Open Guide: {guideKey} | Search: group chat, earshot, or voice
topics.tags: talk speaking address all nearby owned companions souls soul party earshot voice microphone dictation everyone guys

topics.title: Stop
topics.summary: Immediately cancels whatever the bot is doing.
topics.answer: Look at me and press \, or type /bot stop {bot}. I drop whatever I was doing and wait for your next order.
details: Use this if the bot behavior is wrong or unsafe.
Stop clears the current task and lets you issue a new one.
topics.tags: cancel halt panic

topics.title: Stand Down
topics.summary: Bot pauses follow + drop-sweep for 60s, then auto-resumes follow.
topics.answer: Hold \ while looking at me and press 1, or type /bot standdown {bot}. I leave drops alone and stay out of your way for 60 seconds, then go back to following you.
details: Use when you're sniping mobs and don't want the bot running out to grab XP, drops, or chase.
Different from Stop: Stop clears all state. Stand Down keeps the follow target so the bot rejoins formation when the timer expires.
Drop-sweep is suppressed for the full 60s, so drops on the ground are left alone.
Issuing any other command (stop, follow, come) cancels the auto-resume.
topics.shortcuts: Shortcut: hold \ → press 1 (Stand Down looked-at bot)
topics.tags: stand down hold position pause follow xp orb drop

topics.title: Resume
topics.summary: Resumes a paused pending task when available.
topics.answer: Type /bot resume {bot}. If I have a paused task saved, I pick it back up. If I don't, nothing happens.
details: If the bot asks whether to resume or stop, Resume continues that saved task.
If no pending task exists, the command safely does nothing.
topics.shortcuts: Shortcut: (optional) bind Resume key in controls
topics.tags: continue paused task

topics.title: Switch Active Bot (Inventory)
topics.summary: Cycle to another companion from the inventory UI without retyping commands.
topics.answer: In a fren's inventory, press [ or ] to switch to the previous or next fren. You can also click the arrows on the switch chip.
details: In Bot Inventory, press [ and ] to switch previous/next companion.
You can also click < / > in the switch chip on the bot stats row or overlay header.
Switching reuses /bot open <alias>, so normal ownership and permission rules still apply.
topics.command: bot open <alias> (or /bot open for last targeted)
topics.tags: switch inventory open alias multi bot

topics.title: Bot Controls Panel
topics.summary: Configure spawn behavior and per-bot preferences in one place.
topics.answer: Open my inventory, go to the Admin tab and click Bot Controls, or type /configMan. Spawning, dialogue, survival, behaviour and pathfinding settings are all there.
details: Open from Admin tab: Bot Controls >.
Spawn modes are Questing and Admin.
General settings include Global Text Dialogue and Global Voiced Dialogue toggles.
Also includes gameplay, survival, behavior, and pathfinder toggles.
Use this as the primary settings hub instead of memorizing many commands.
See also: Modes topics for progression context.
topics.shortcuts: Actions overlay: Admin tab > Bot Controls >
topics.tags: bot controls settings spawn mode admin panel

topics.title: Auto Spawn on Load
topics.summary: Controls whether a bot automatically returns when you re-enter the world.
topics.answer: When it's on, I come back by myself when you load the world. Type /bot despawn {bot} to shelve me until you spawn me again, or /bot despawn session to send me away for this session only. The toggle is in Bot Controls under Spawning.
details: When ON (default), the bot spawns automatically on world load with full state restored.
When OFF, the bot stays shelved until you manually run /bot spawn.
Use /bot despawn to shelve a bot across sessions (turns this OFF).
Use /bot despawn session to remove a bot for the current session only (does not change this setting).
Toggle this in the Bot Controls panel under the Spawning tab.
topics.tags: shelve shelved auto spawn load world session despawn persist

topics.title: Auto Respawn
topics.summary: Controls what happens when a bot dies.
topics.answer: When it's on, I respawn right away at my bed, my base or the world spawn. When it's off, I ask in chat whether to respawn and you answer yes or no. The toggle is in Bot Controls under Spawning.
details: When ON (default), the bot respawns instantly at the world spawn / bed / saved base.
When OFF, the bot's death triggers a chat prompt: 'Respawn now? (yes/no)'. Reply yes to bring them back, no to stand down.
If you don't answer before the session ends, the bot stays shelved. Use /bot spawn <name> or toggle Auto Respawn back ON to bring them back.
Toggling Auto Respawn ON while a bot is shelved auto-spawns them, which is useful as a revive shortcut.
topics.tags: respawn death auto prompt revive

topics.title: Bot Roster (Spawn Bots…)
topics.summary: Multi-select screen for (re)spawning bots and creating new ones.
topics.answer: Open Bot Controls and click Spawn Bots, or press - while no frens are out. Tick the frens you want and click Spawn Selected, or type a new name to make a new fren.
details: Opens automatically after you pick Admin Mode on a fresh world, or when you press the [-] go-to-look hotkey while no bots are present.
You can also open it any time from Bot Controls → 'Spawn Bots…' button in the footer.
Tick one or more saved bots and click 'Spawn Selected (N)'. They spawn in a ring around your look position so they don't pile up.

Create a brand-new bot with the name input field. Names follow Minecraft username rules (letters, numbers, _-.', max 24 chars). Random skin is assigned. Customize later via the bot's inventory → skin chooser.
The 'Manage settings → Bot Controls' link at the bottom opens the full Bot Controls panel for per-bot spawning rules.
topics.shortcuts: Bot Controls > Spawn Bots…, also the [-] key when no bots exist
topics.tags: roster restore multi select spawn multiple checkbox create new bot skin

topics.title: Bulk Apply (All Bots)
topics.summary: One-click reset buttons that set a spawning flag for every bot in this world.
topics.answer: Expand the global settings in Bot Controls and use the Bulk Apply buttons at the bottom. They set Auto Respawn or Auto Spawn on Load for every fren at once, and you can still change each fren afterwards.
details: Expand the global toggles panel in Bot Controls to find them at the bottom.
Auto Respawn: All Bots [ALL ON] / [ALL OFF]: resets the per-bot Auto Respawn flag for every bot. ALL ON also auto-spawns any inactive bot that was waiting on a respawn decision.
Auto Spawn on Load: All Bots [ALL ON] / [ALL OFF]: resets the per-bot Auto Spawn on Load flag for every bot.
These are reset buttons, not persistent toggles. They just apply the value and exit. Per-bot settings you tweak later still take precedence.
topics.shortcuts: Bot Controls > Global Settings (expanded) > Bulk Apply
topics.tags: bulk apply reset all bots mass global

topics.title: No-Companions HUD Hint
topics.summary: The on-screen notice that appears when no bots are currently in the world.
topics.answer: That notice shows when no frens are in the world. Press - to open the Bot Roster and spawn one, or click the small x to hide it for this session.
details: Shown after ~2 seconds of no bots being present, in admin mode or when survival recruitment is complete.
Press [-] (the go-to-look key) while no bots are present to jump straight to the Bot Roster. Any time, open Guide (]) > Admin > Bot Controls > Spawn Bots.
Once a bot is out, [-] sends it where you look instead.
Click the small [x] button on the hint to hide it for the rest of the session.
It will reappear the next time bots transition from present → absent (e.g. everyone dies or you /bot despawn them).
topics.tags: no bots hint notification hud dismiss close x session

topics.title: World Mode Reset
topics.summary: Admin command to re-trigger the world mode selection (Questing vs Admin) welcome screen.
topics.answer: An operator types /bot worldmode reset, then rejoins the world or presses the roster key, and the world mode screen opens again.
details: Useful when a recreated world inherits the old mode-selection state (save-path collision) and the welcome screen doesn't reappear.
Run /bot worldmode reset. You'll get a chat confirmation.
Then press the open-roster hotkey (or rejoin) and the mode selection screen will open again.
Requires bot command permission (admin).
topics.tags: worldmode world mode reset welcome questing admin reopen

topics.title: Follow
topics.summary: Keeps the bot near you while you travel.
topics.answer: Look at me and press the backtick key, or type /bot follow {bot}. Press it again to stop. The Actions menu sets how close I stay.
details: Great for cave runs and travel support.
Use follow distance controls in Actions to tighten or loosen spacing.
topics.tags: trail escort companion

topics.title: Keep Bots Quiet
topics.summary: Turn down what bots say, in text or out loud.
topics.answer: Open Bot Controls and turn off the dialogue toggles you don't want. Scripted Text and Scripted Voice cover the ready-made lines, and Soul Chat and Soul Voice cover AI chat. Each one works on its own.
details: Open Bot Controls and find the dialogue toggles.
Scripted Text and Scripted Voice cover the ready-made lines.
Soul Chat and Soul Voice cover AI chat, if you set it up.
Each toggle works alone, so you can keep text and turn off voice.
topics.tags: quiet mute silence stop talking chatter voice text dialogue

topics.title: Let a Friend Use Bots
topics.summary: Who can command a bot on a shared world.
topics.answer: A fren listens to its owner, an operator or the host. To let a friend command your frens, make them an operator on the world.
details: A bot's owner, an operator or the host can command it.
To let a friend command your bots, make them an operator on the world.
topics.tags: friend guest lan multiplayer share permission operator op

topics.title: Follow Teleport
topics.summary: Wolf-style catch-up teleport during follow mode.
topics.answer: Turn on Follow Teleport in Bot Controls under Behavior. While I follow you, I teleport to a safe spot near you when you are 15 or more blocks away and out of my sight, when I am stuck for about a second and a half, or when you are out of sight 10 or more blocks above or below me.
details: When enabled, the bot teleports near you when it is 15 or more blocks away and can't see you, when it is stuck for about 1.5 seconds at least 7 blocks away, when you are out of sight 10 or more blocks above or below it, or when it is 20 or more blocks away and stuck for a second.
This only affects follow mode. It does not enable teleport during skills, sweeps, or other behaviors.
The bot finds a safe spot behind you, so it won't teleport into lava or off cliffs.
Toggle in Bot Controls > Behavior > Follow Teleport.
Admins can control which players see this toggle in Player Settings.
topics.tags: follow teleport wolf catch-up warp tp stuck lost

topics.title: Regroup
topics.summary: Calls the companion back toward you using the safer regroup behavior.
topics.answer: Type /bot regroup {bot} and I come back to you the careful way. Use it when following goes wrong or you want me close right now.
details: Use this when follow is struggling or you want the bot to come back to you deliberately.
Preferred command: /bot regroup. Legacy alias: /bot come.
Safe regroup avoids the more aggressive recovery behavior used by the older come wording.
topics.tags: regroup come stuck follow recovery

topics.title: Return Home
topics.summary: Sends the bot back to its saved home/base anchor.
topics.answer: Type /bot return {bot} and I head back to my home base. Run it again to cancel.
details: Toggle style: pressing again can cancel and return control.
Pair with Guard/Patrol for base security loops.
topics.tags: home base return

topics.title: Guard & Patrol
topics.summary: Keeps the bot at a spot, guarding it, patrolling around it or staying put.
topics.answer: Open Actions, Orders & Travel and press Guard or Patrol, or type /bot guard {bot}. I hold the spot where I stand and fight mobs that come after me. Give me a bow and arrows if you want me to shoot mobs that are after you.
details: Guard stands at the spot, patrol walks around it, and /bot stay waits where it is. Press the button again to stop.
The + and - buttons set the radius, 3 to 32 blocks. Changing it resets the centre to where the bot stands.
It notices hostile mobs it can see within about 10 blocks, whatever the radius.
With only melee weapons it fights mobs that are after it. With a bow, crossbow or trident it also attacks other hostile mobs, and defends your pets and village villagers.
It chases what it fights and walks back afterwards. It doesn't retreat when hurt, so give it armour, a shield and food. It does back away from creepers.
The order isn't saved. After a restart or a death, give it again.
It stays out through the night unless both Auto Home @ Sunset and Sunset Return in Guard/Patrol are on (Actions, Automation).
topics.tags: guard patrol stay defend protect post sentry radius

topics.title: Cleanup (Drop Sweep)
topics.summary: Collects nearby dropped items quickly.
topics.answer: Press Cleanup in the Actions menu, or type /bot skill drop_sweep {bot}, and I pick up the items lying around nearby. It helps after a fight, a mining trip or a big tree run.
details: Best after combat, mining, logging, or building.
Runs a focused pickup sweep to reduce item despawns.
topics.tags: drop sweep pickup

topics.title: Retrieve Drops
topics.summary: Sends the bot to where you or another bot last died to pick up the items, then it comes back to you.
topics.answer: Press Retrieve Drops in my menu, or type /bot retrieve {bot} me. I fast-travel to where you died, pick up what you dropped and bring it back to you. Items only last about 5 minutes on the ground, so send me quickly and give me food for the trip.
details: The bot fast travels to a safe spot next to the death position, even in another dimension. The travel rest time does not apply, but it still needs food for the trip.

It goes after the items that dropped when you or the bot died, tells you how many items it got, and fast travels back to you. Other items it walks over may still be picked up. If its inventory fills up it stops and says so. It never stores items in chests there.
It lands on a safe spot near you. If you are offline, it can't travel back, it finds no safe spot near you, or the sweep fails twice, it stays at the death spot and tells you.
Items on the ground last about 5 minutes while the area is loaded. For a death older than 20 minutes, or one whose time is unknown, it still goes but warns that the items may be gone.
Deaths in lava or the void are refused because the items are gone, and so is any death while the keep inventory game rule is on. A death to a mob or in fire is allowed, with a warning.
Only the bot's owner can send it, and only for their own death or one of their own bots.
topics.shortcuts: Actions menu: Retrieve Drops (your own death)
topics.tags: retrieve death died drops items lost recover corpse grave fetch

topics.title: Fishing
topics.summary: Fish until sunset or a chosen catch count.
topics.answer: Type /bot skill fish {bot} and I fish until sunset, or add a number, like /bot skill fish 20 {bot}, to stop after that many catches. The +/- buttons in the Actions menu set the count too.
details: Set a custom count from the Actions row +/- controls.
When count is unset, fishing runs by default behavior.
topics.tags: fish food water

topics.title: Forget Fishing Spot
topics.summary: Clears the bot's saved fishing stand so it picks a fresh spot next time.
topics.answer: Type /bot fish forget {bot}, or press Forget Spot under Fishing. I forget my saved fishing stand and pick a fresh spot next time. Your lodestone compasses stay as they are.
details: When a bot is mid-session the sunset auto-return saves the current stand so it can resume there at sunrise.
If the saved spot is bad (unreachable, no nearby chest, unsafe shoreline), the bot can end up fast-travelling back to it every morning and failing.
Running this clears the saved session and the sunrise-resume record for the target bot.

Lodestone compasses are NOT touched. The next /bot fish walks to a fishing spot it remembers within 64 blocks, or finds water near where it stands. It doesn't use a compass for that: on its own it uses one only to go home at sunset and back to work at sunrise (see Daily Work Loops).
topics.tags: fish forget clear reset spot session resume

topics.title: Woodcut
topics.summary: Fells nearby trees. Defaults to 'Until sunset' mode. Use +/- to set a specific tree count.
topics.answer: Type /bot skill woodcut {bot} and I cut trees until sunset, or add a number to cut that many trees. I won't cut trees inside your base, the spawn area, a protected zone or a mapped village. Give me an axe, or I punch a tree and make one.
details: At the default (Until sunset), the bot cuts trees until dusk then stops.
Use +/- to set a minimum tree count instead.
Use Cleanup after large runs to gather leftovers quickly.
Bots won't cut trees inside your base, the Spawn area, a protected area or a mapped village. If those are the only trees nearby, the bot walks out to find others.
An admin can let bots cut Spawn area trees in Admin, World Settings.
No axe? The bot punches a tree for wood, then makes a crafting table, sticks and a wooden axe.
topics.tags: tree lumber logs axe protected base spawn walks away far

topics.title: Daily Work Loops (Lodestone Compass)
topics.summary: Send a fren to a far work spot that it returns to every morning: home at sunset, back to work at sunrise.
topics.answer: Put a lodestone at the work spot, bind a compass to it and put the compass in my inventory. Then start the job with no count, like /bot skill woodcut {bot}. I go home at sunset and fast-travel back to that lodestone at sunrise, as long as I stopped within 128 blocks of it and have food.
details: Put a lodestone at the work spot (a forest, a fishing shore), bind a compass to it, and give the compass to the fren. Name your compasses on an anvil to tell them apart.
Give the fren somewhere to sleep: a base or a bed it has slept in (see Home & Bases Explained). With neither, it goes to the world spawn.
Start the job with no count, for example /bot skill woodcut {bot} or /bot skill fish {bot}. A job with a count ends when the count is reached and is not picked up again.

At sunset the fren stops, remembers the job and where it stopped, and goes home. It remembers the job when it holds a compass whose lodestone still stands in this dimension (or when it is at a base, or sheltered in place).
With any lodestone compass in its pack, it fast-travels home at sunset instead of walking, when home is at least 16 blocks away.

At sunrise it fast-travels to the lodestone nearest the spot where it stopped, lands beside it and starts the same job again. That lodestone must be within 128 blocks of the spot. If none is, it starts the job again wherever it woke up. Hunting has its own loop and is not resumed this way.
Fast travel still needs a gate (a bound lodestone compass is one) and food. See Fast-Travel Gates.
If a lodestone is broken, the compass stops working: /bot compass list {bot} shows each compass and any that lost their lodestone.
topics.shortcuts: Inventory > Bases button (white rows are lodestone compasses)
topics.tags: loop loops automation routine daily repeat every day morning sunrise sunset resume lodestone compass woodcut fish work spot far

topics.title: Wool
topics.summary: Shears sheep and gathers wool.
topics.answer: Set a target with the +/- buttons in the Actions menu and press Wool, or type /bot skill wool <count> {bot}. I shear the sheep around me, so it works best in open fields with sheep nearby.
details: Use +/- to specify a target amount.
Works best in open areas with nearby sheep.
topics.tags: sheep wool

topics.title: Leaf Litter
topics.summary: Collects leaf litter from the ground for cheap furnace fuel.
topics.answer: Press Leaf Litter in the Actions menu, or type /bot skill leaf_litter {bot}. I collect up to a stack of leaf litter, the cheapest furnace fuel. Forests have the most.
details: Works best in forested biomes where leaf litter is abundant.
Leaf litter is the cheapest fuel, always preferred over logs or coal.
Manual command collects up to a full stack, idle hobby collects a few.
topics.tags: leaf litter fuel kindling fire forest

topics.title: Build Farm
topics.summary: Builds a watered square farm and plants it.
topics.answer: Press Farming in the Actions menu and pick the spot, or type /bot skill farm {bot}. I need a hoe, seeds and a bucket. I build a square of farmland around a small pool and till one plot for each seed I carry.
details: Builds a 10 by 10 square of farmland around a 2 by 2 pool, so every plot stays watered.
Tills only as many plots as it has seeds. Give it more seeds for a bigger farm.
Needs a hoe, seeds and a bucket in its inventory. It fills buckets from water nearby and doesn't take tools or seeds from chests.
The Farming button shows a preview where you look. The lock key fixes it so the arrow keys can move it, and the Go To Look key starts the build.
With the command it looks for an existing walled 2 by 2 pool within 24 blocks, or picks a flat, open spot itself.
Clears trees and levels the ground. It adds no fences or torches, and runs once.
topics.tags: crop irrigation agriculture build

topics.title: Plant Seeds
topics.summary: Plants seeds on empty farmland nearby.
topics.answer: Type /bot skill plant {bot} and I plant seeds in empty farmland within 16 blocks. I don't till, so the farmland has to be there. I can plant wheat, beetroot, melon, pumpkin, potato and carrot.
details: Plants empty farmland within 16 blocks. It doesn't till new ground.
Supports wheat, beetroot, melon, pumpkin, potato, and carrot, from its own inventory.
There is no button for it. Harvest Crops also plants empty farmland.
topics.tags: seed plant crop sow farming

topics.title: Harvest Crops
topics.summary: Harvests ripe wheat, beetroot, carrots and potatoes, and replants them.
topics.answer: Press Harvest in the Actions menu, or type /bot skill harvest {bot}. I harvest ripe wheat, beetroot, carrots and potatoes within 16 blocks, replant them and pick up the drops. If my pack fills, I empty it into a chest.
details: Harvests fully grown wheat, beetroot, carrots and potatoes within 16 blocks. Not melons, pumpkins or other crops.
Won't break crops inside a mapped village.
Replants each plot, then plants any other empty farmland nearby.
Stands beside the crops, and sneaks when it has to stand on farmland, so it doesn't trample them.
Can ask to take seeds from a chest near it to finish replanting.
With fewer than 3 free slots it empties its pack into a nearby chest, or places one. It keeps its seeds, carrots and potatoes for replanting.
Runs once. Run it again when the crops are ripe.
topics.tags: harvest reap crop gather farming mature

topics.title: Collect Dirt
topics.summary: Collects dirt-like blocks for scaffolding and builds.
topics.answer: Type /bot skill collect_dirt {bot}, with a number if you want a set amount. I dig dirt-like blocks for building and scaffolding.
details: Useful prep for construction and terrain patching.
Command supports optional target amount.
topics.tags: dirt scaffold

topics.title: Stripmine
topics.summary: Mines a straight tunnel for ores and stone resources.
topics.answer: Set the tunnel length with the +/- buttons in the Actions menu, face the way you want me to dig and press the Go To key (- by default). The command is /bot skill stripmine <length> {bot}.
details: Use +/- to set desired tunnel length.
Then face the way to dig and press the Go To key (- by default) to start.
The bot should refuse impossible or unsafe tool scenarios.
topics.tags: tunnel ore

topics.title: Ascent
topics.summary: Climbs upward by a block count or until surface sky.
topics.answer: Set a block count with the +/- buttons, or turn on the ☀ toggle to go all the way to the surface, then press the Go To key (- by default). The command is /bot skill mining ascent <blocks> {bot}, or surface in place of the number.
details: Use +/- for block count.
Then press the Go To key (- by default) to start.
Use the ☀ toggle in Actions to turn Surface mode on/off.
topics.tags: up climb surface

topics.title: Descent
topics.summary: Digs downward by a selected block count.
topics.answer: Set the depth with the +/- buttons, face the way you want me to dig and press the Go To key (- by default). The command is /bot skill mining descent <blocks> {bot}.
details: Use +/- to set depth target.
Then face the way to dig and press the Go To key (- by default) to start.
Good for controlled shaft digging with oversight.
topics.tags: down dig shaft

topics.title: Fortify Village
topics.summary: Builds a stone wall with corner towers and a gate around a village.
topics.answer: Bring me to a village, give me stone bricks or cobblestone, and use Actions, Construction, Fortify Village or type /bot fortify {bot}. I build a wall with towers and a gate 12 blocks outside the houses. The moat is a separate step, Fortify Moat.
details: Finds villagers, beds and workstations within 64 blocks, draws an outline around them and builds 12 blocks outside it.
The wall is one block thick and about three and a half blocks high, with a tower at each corner and a gate on the longest side.
Builds only from its own inventory: stone bricks, cobblestone, stone, cobbled deepslate, andesite or dirt. Planks can't be used.
The moat is a separate step (Fortify Moat). It digs the ditch and fills open gaps in the planned lining. It does not replace dirt or stone with a stone lining.
The finish report counts the wall, towers and gatehouse only. Below 85% it says Partial, and patch fills the gaps.
Resume skips towers. Patch finishes them and fixes damage.
dry_run: preview the layout with particles. status: per-side progress, missing blocks shown in red.
drift / expand / merge / list / name: manage saved walls. Expand only grows a wall.
Tip: Use the Bases screen (Wall Manager) for a wall's buttons, ownership and access.
topics.tags: fortify village wall defense perimeter tower gatehouse resume patch status merge hull particles

topics.title: Fast-Travel Gates
topics.summary: Which items/conditions let the bot fast-travel, and at what speed.
topics.answer: The quickest way to let me fast-travel is a lodestone compass in my pack or an Eye of Ender with either of us. A map and compass that show the destination also work, more slowly. Without one of these I can't fast-travel, and I tell you why.
details: §eTier 2 (1.0×, instant-class)§r: any one of these alone qualifies:
• Bot holds a §flodestone compass bound to a target§r
• Bot §for§r owner has an §fEye of Ender§r
• Bot §for§r owner has a §fWizard's Tome§r
• Bot §for§r owner is within 6 blocks of an §fEnchanting Table§r
• §fBoth§r bot and owner hold §fEnder Pearls§r
§eSurface Tier 1§r: needs at least one gate (Tier 2 unmet):
• §fMap + Compass§r and destination pixel rendered on one of the bot's maps, OR
• §fSmoke signal§r: destination is inside a labeled base, lit campfire on hay at base centre, bot within 5× base radius
• §fSpyglass§r in bot inventory shaves one tier step
• 1 gate → 3.0× delay, 2 gates → 2.0× delay
§eUnderground§r (stricter):
• Map + Compass §fplus torch/lantern§r → 2.0×
• Lodestone compass without bound target → 2.0×
• Smoke signal within §f2× base radius§r → 3.0× (tight range)
• Otherwise refused, bot walks

§cNote:§r these gates apply to automatic fast-travel (sunset return, sunrise resume, /bot home). The §fSummon§r button in the spellbook uses the Eye of Ender (60s cooldown) as its own gate. The §fRemote Guidance§r and §fChorus Recall§r spells in Bot Inventory are separate manual spells with their own pearl/chorus costs.
Chat tells you which gate activated each time fast-travel fires, so you can tune your setup.
topics.shortcuts: See chat when bot departs: '(fast-travel: ...)' tag
topics.tags: fast travel gates lodestone compass eye ender enchanting table smoke signal map tier delay

topics.title: Home & Bases Explained
topics.summary: Two kinds of rows in the Base Manager, and two meanings of [Home].
topics.answer: Yellow rows in the Base Manager are bases, and white rows are lodestone compasses I carry. At sunset I go to the closest of my last bed, my preferred home base and my nearest base, so mark the one you want with Set Home and keep me near it.
details: §eYellow [Base]§r rows are registered bases, saved locations with a protection radius (r=40). Use 'Set Home' to mark one as the bot's preferred home.
§fWhite rows§r are lodestone compasses in the bot's inventory. They have no protection. They're just named travel targets.
[Home] before a §eyellow§r name = this base is the bot's §epreferred home§r. Used by sunset-return and most 'go home' logic.
[Home] before a §fwhite§r name = this lodestone compass is the bot's §edesignated home compass§r. Used by the fast-travel mechanics.
You can have a preferred home base AND a designated home compass at the same time. They are independent.
Sunset-return picks the CLOSEST of: last-slept bed, preferred home, or nearest base. If your preferred home is far away and Spawn is closer, the bot may go to Spawn instead.
To force a specific base on return, either delete the closer alternatives or keep the bot geographically near the preferred home.
Admins can set who owns a base with /bot base owner <base> <player|server|none>. Put base names with spaces in quotes, for example /bot base owner "My Base" server. Operators and the host only.
topics.tags: home base lodestone compass preferred yellow white explained legend

topics.title: Map Village
topics.summary: Saves the nearby settlement as a shared remembered no-go zone without building a wall.
topics.answer: Open the Base Manager, go to the Villages section and map the village you're in. Frens then won't mine, cut trees, dig or hunt passive mobs inside it.
details: Open the Base Manager and use the Villages section to map the local settlement.
The saved village reuses the fortification convex hull and stores it by name.
Mapped villages are global shared data for the world, not personal claims.
Bots avoid mapped villages for mining, woodcutting, dirt collection, flower/mushroom/grass gathering, and passive-mob hunting.
Village rows appear in the same manager list as bases and walls, but they are not valid home or go-to targets.
topics.tags: village mapping perimeter convex hull no-go zone bases manager

topics.summary: Layman progression path: recruit first, then unlock more capabilities.
topics.answer: In Questing mode you recruit frens in a village and unlock more as the friendship grows. The dialogue topics tell you what unlocks next.
details: Designed for survival progression and narrative onboarding.
Dialogue topics help explain what is unlocked next.

topics.title: Delegate Mode Setup
topics.summary: Admins can permit specific non-operator players to choose world mode.
topics.answer: An operator types /bot recruit mode_access allow <player> to let that player choose the world mode. Use revoke to take it back, or clear to remove everyone, for this world.
details: Use mode_access allow/revoke to manage delegated players.
Operators can always choose mode. Delegates are world-specific.
Clear removes all delegates for the current world.

topics.summary: Spawn/use bots with broad capabilities immediately.
topics.answer: In Admin mode you make frens yourself with the Bot Roster or /bot spawn <name> admin, and they can do everything right away, with no recruiting.
details: Best for testing, admin workflows, and sandbox play.
No recruitment progression needed.

topics.answer: Learning Mode is an operator tool that records how you play so bot control can be tuned later. Use /bot learn status, start and stop. It doesn't change what I can do.

Captured traces can include movement, camera, interactions, and local context for analysis.

topics.title: Wizard's Tome
topics.summary: A rare magical item that unlocks the companion movement spells from anywhere.
topics.answer: Craft it in The End: hold an Eye of Ender, carry a book, a diamond, 3 redstone and 3 lapis, and sneak-right-click a fully powered enchanting table with 15 bookshelves. All of those items are used up. Carry it, stand near me and press [ to open the spells.
details: Crafted via ritual: sneak-right-click an Enchanting Table in The End.
Requires a fully powered table (15 bookshelves).
Hold an Eye of Ender and have in inventory: 1 Book, 1 Diamond, 3 Redstone, 3 Lapis Lazuli. All of them, the Eye included, are used up.
Once crafted, carry it and press [ near the bot. It unlocks Regroup, Summon (also across dimensions), Home and Remote Inventory.
Can also be obtained via /give @p frens:wizard_tome in creative.
topics.shortcuts: Open Spells key [ (works in any world)

topics.title: Command + Keybind Cheatsheet
topics.summary: Quick reference for the most-used controls.
topics.answer: The main keys are {guideKey} for the Guide, backtick to toggle follow, \ to stop me, - to send me where you look and [ for spells. Hold \ for the hotkey menu. You can rebind them all in Minecraft's Controls screen.
details: Guide -> {guideKey} -> open in-game companion guide
Follow toggle -> ` -> bot follow toggle <bot>
Go to look / context action -> - -> go_to_look, recruitment contact, or spells (depends on context)
Switch bot in inventory -> [ / ] -> previous / next companion
Sleep -> (hold \ then 5) -> bot sleep <bot>
Send your bots to bed -> type zzz in chat -> admins choose (Log Off If Can't Sleep) if a bot that can't find or make a bed logs off for the night and comes back at dawn
Stop -> \ -> bot stop <bot>
Leash / tether helper -> ' -> leash action when available
Let go of leads -> Release Leads in the bot menu -> bot leash release <bot>
Fetch your drops after dying -> Retrieve Drops in the bot menu -> bot retrieve <bot> me
Resume -> (bind key.frens.resume) -> bot resume <bot>
Open Spells -> [ -> opens the Spells tab of your bot inventory in any world (rebind key.frens.open_spells)
Recruit Contact -> (optional bind key.frens.recruit_contact) -> opens recruitment contact flow
Tip: hold Stop (\) for the 1-0 hotkey overlay menu.
topics.command: bot follow toggle <bot> | bot go_to_look | bot stop <bot> | bot resume <bot>
topics.shortcuts: Minecraft Controls: Follow, Go To Look, Open Guide, Stop, Leash, Resume, Open Spells, Recruit Contact
topics.tags: shortcut hotkey keybind follow stop goto go to look leash release leads lead retrieve death drops

topics.title: Navigation Artifacts
topics.summary: Give your companion a Compass, Map, or Eye of Ender to unlock autonomous navigation.
topics.answer: Put a map and compass, a lodestone compass or an Eye of Ender in my inventory and I can fast-travel instead of walking. A lodestone compass or an Eye of Ender is the fastest. None of them get used up.
details: Compass / Map (basic): bot can navigate to its nearest or preferred base, same dimension only.
Eye of Ender (enhanced): navigate to any named base, cross-dimension, at full fast-travel speed. Either you or the bot can hold it.
Use /bot open <alias> to give items to your companion via its inventory screen.
Navigation artifacts are reusable. They are not consumed.
topics.shortcuts: Give item via Bot Inventory screen
topics.tags: compass map eye ender navigation artifact tier

topics.title: Remote Guidance
topics.summary: Uses paired ender pearls to guide your companion across any distance.
topics.answer: We both need an Ender Pearl. Open the Spells tab with [, pick Remote Guidance and choose your location, my home or a base. Both pearls are used up when you cast, and I fast-travel there, after my rest if I just travelled, unless I'm fighting.
details: Both you and your companion need at least one Ender Pearl somewhere in your inventories.
Choose destination: your location, its home, or one of your bases.
Both pearls are used up when you cast, before the trip is checked.

It is a fast travel trip with no food needed. A fight cancels it and the pearls are lost. If it is resting from a trip, it leaves when the rest ends. It also needs a way to find the place. Carry a spare pearl each so the pearls still count as that way.
The trip takes about 1.5 seconds per chunk, more across dimensions.
Open the Spells tab to cast this spell.
topics.tags: spell guidance ender pearl paired navigation remote

topics.title: Chorus Recall
topics.summary: Consumes paired ender pearls and chorus fruit for an instant teleport.
topics.answer: We each need an Ender Pearl and a Chorus Fruit. Open the Spells tab with [ and pick Chorus Recall to teleport me to you or you to me, instantly and across dimensions. All four items are used up.
details: Both you and your companion need one Ender Pearl and one Chorus Fruit somewhere in their inventories.
Choose direction: teleport bot to you, or you to bot.
Works across dimensions. Always instant, no delay.
All four items are consumed (one pearl + one chorus from each).
A bot riding an animal may be refused, with nothing used up.
topics.tags: spell recall chorus fruit ender pearl teleport instant paired

topics.title: Fast Travel & Navigation Tiers
topics.summary: Companion fast travel speed depends on held artifacts.
topics.answer: There's no speed setting. I fast-travel at full speed with a lodestone compass, or when either of us has an Eye of Ender or a Wizard's Tome. A map and compass that show the destination work too, more slowly, and with nothing I walk.
details: Full speed: the bot holds a bound lodestone compass, the bot or you hold an Eye of Ender or a Wizard's Tome, the bot or you are within 6 blocks of an Enchanting Table, or the bot and you both hold Ender Pearls.
Slower: the bot holds a Map and Compass that show the destination (underground it also needs a torch or lantern), or a smoke signal marks the destination base.
There is no walk or fast-travel setting. Without a gate the bot walks.
Cross-dimension travel adds 30 seconds. Delays run from 7 seconds to 5 minutes.
topics.shortcuts: Give the bot a Map and Compass for basic travel. For full speed, give the bot a bound lodestone compass, or carry an Eye of Ender yourself (one in the bot's inventory works too). See Fast-Travel Gates for every gate.
topics.tags: navigation fast travel tier map compass eye ender artifact speed

topics.title: Preserve Expensive Gear
topics.summary: Keep your bots from wearing out your best tools.
topics.answer: Turn on Preserve Expensive Gear in my Admin tab, Behavior section. Then I stop using enchanted, gold, diamond, netherite or turtle shell gear below 11% durability, or 3% in a fight, and swap to something cheaper. It applies to all your frens.
details: When enabled, your bots refuse to use enchanted items and gear made of gold, diamond, netherite, or turtle shell once durability drops below 11%.
In combat, the threshold drops to 3%, so the bot will push a risky item harder when lives are on the line.
When a tool is locked out, the bot tries to swap to a cheaper alternative from its inventory, walks to a registered chest for a replacement, or crafts a new one at a nearby crafting table.
If nothing is available, the bot pauses and speaks up. Check its inventory and give it a refill.
Note on Mending: items with the Mending enchantment are also preserved. If you want a Mending item used continuously for XP self-repair, disable this toggle.
Toggle this under the bot's Admin tab → Behavior section. The setting is per player and applies to every bot you own. Default: OFF.
topics.tags: durability tools gear preserve diamond netherite gold enchanted expensive shield armor mending

topics.title: Spell Ingredients
topics.summary: Quick reference for all spell-related items and what they unlock.
topics.answer: A Wizard's Tome, or standing near an enchanting table, lets you Regroup, Summon, send me Home and open my inventory from anywhere. An Eye of Ender gives Regroup, Summon and Home. Paired Ender Pearls cast Remote Guidance, and pearls plus chorus fruit cast Chorus Recall.
details: Wizard's Tome (you or the bot carry it): Regroup, Summon (also across dimensions), Home and Remote Inventory.
Enchanting Table within 4 blocks: the same as the Tome. For Summon across dimensions it must be near you.
The Tome and table don't replace the pearls, chorus fruit, table or anvil the other spells need.
Eye of Ender (you or the bot): Regroup, Summon and Home. Not used up. Summon with your own Eye and no Tome or table has a 60s cooldown.
Goat Horn (you carry it): Regroup by typed command only. The Spells tab greys Regroup out with only a horn.
Ender Pearl (one each): Remote Guidance, used up.
Ender Pearl + Chorus Fruit (one each): Chorus Recall, instant teleport, used up.
Soul of Ender: the bot needs an Eye of Ender and a Chorus Fruit. The fruit is used up.
Enchant and Anvil need you within 4 blocks of the block.
topics.shortcuts: Hold item or be near Enchanting Table to unlock spells
topics.tags: spell ingredient wizard tome eye ender pearl chorus goat horn enchanting

topics.title: Quick Store & Quick Fetch
topics.summary: Point at a nearby chest and click to deposit or take items.
topics.answer: Open Actions, Core Actions, then Quick Store or Quick Fetch, point at a chest and left-click. I walk over and put my items in, or take them out. Shift-click Quick Store to empty everything, armour and tools too.
details: Quick Store: Actions → Core Actions → Quick Store. Bot walks to the chest and deposits.
Quick Fetch: Actions → Core Actions → Quick Fetch. Bot walks to the chest and takes items into its inventory.
Point at any container (chest, barrel, shulker box) and left-click to confirm.
Quick Store, plain click: deposits loose items, keeps tools, weapons and armor, bundles, torches, arrows, leads, compasses, clocks, and cooked food, bread and stews.

Quick Store, shift+click: dumps everything (including armor, tools, and food). Use when swapping loadouts. Both stop putting in building blocks once the bot holds 32 or fewer, so it can usually still climb out of holes.
The bot physically walks to the chest before interacting. It must be within 32 blocks, not busy with a task and not in a fight.
If the chest fills up (store) or the bot’s inventory fills up (fetch), remaining items stay put.
The bot does NOT remember chests used this way. Only automated-task chests appear in Storage.
Right-click to cancel targeting mode.
The bot can be interrupted with /bot stop. Items are never dropped on the ground.
topics.shortcuts: Works with any container block within 6 blocks of your crosshair
topics.tags: quick store fetch deposit withdraw chest point click target container

topics.title: Hunting
topics.summary: Hunts animals for food and leather, or zombies when well armed, then cooks the meat.
topics.answer: Open Actions, Utilities, Hunting, pick an animal and press Hunt, or type /bot skill hunt 5 cow {bot}. You have to kill one of a kind yourself before I can hunt it. I leave babies, pets, named animals and animals inside bases alone.
details: Tick one type per hunt. Ticking several hunts only one of them, and ticks also limit hunts that name no mob.
Count sets how many. Leave it empty to hunt until nightfall. A hunt with a count keeps going through the night.
Zone sets the search range: 48, 80 or 120 blocks.
Depop (on by default) only hunts a type with 3 or more around and stops once fewer than 3 are left.
Animals on a lead are not protected. Keep farm animals in a base, or name them.
Zombies need 8 hearts of health, some armour and a melee weapon.
When a hunt ends normally with at least one kill, it cooks the meat in a nearby furnace or smoker, then goes home.
Auto Hunt (Starving), under Actions, Automation, hunts on its own when the bot is hungry and low on food.
topics.tags: hunt hunting meat food leather cow pig chicken sheep zombie cook depop

topics.title: Storage
topics.summary: View and manage supply chests your companions have placed in the world.
topics.answer: Open Actions, Utilities, Storage to see the chests I've placed. Go sends me to one, Collect has me fetch items from it, and Dismiss removes it from the list without breaking it.
details: Open via Actions → Utilities → Storage.
Each chest shows coordinates, status, and a snapshot of its contents.
Go: fast-travel the bot to the chest location.
Collect: bot fast-travels to chest, takes up to about 256 items, then stays, returns to you, or returns to a base named home (or where it started if there is none).
Dismiss: removes the chest from the registry (does not break the block).
Go and Collect use fast travel, so the bot needs a gate (see Fast-Travel Gates). A lodestone compass or an Eye of Ender gives full speed. A Map and Compass that show the chest is slower.
Hover a chest row to see a tooltip of its last-known contents.

Note: Only chests this bot placed appear here (during a job or for /bot store deposit), in its current dimension. Chests it places while fishing, building a shelter or smelting are not listed. Chests it only used, and Quick Store/Fetch chests, are not tracked.
topics.shortcuts: Switch between bots with the dropdown in the header
topics.tags: storage chest supply collect go dismiss fast travel artifacts

topics.title: Protected Zones
topics.summary: Mark areas where bots cannot break blocks.
topics.answer: An operator types /bot zone wand, right-clicks two corners and presses = to name the zone. My mining jobs stop at its edge, and other players' frens leave it alone.
details: Admins can create protected zones using the Zone Wand.
Get the wand: /bot zone wand or 'New Zone' in the Base Manager.
Right-click a block to set Corner 1, right-click again for Corner 2.
Cyan particles appear showing the zone boundary.
Press [=] to confirm and name the zone.

Stripmine, Collect Dirt, Ascent and Descent stop at every zone, your own included. In your own zones, or zones you are permitted in, the message offers Resume, which lets the job continue for 60 seconds. It isn't offered inside a base that isn't yours (the Spawn base included), inside a fortified wall or its margin, in a mapped village or in a bee nest area, even your own fort or village. Other players' bots won't break blocks in your zones.
Any player can view zone boundaries via Base Manager > Show.
Admins can rename or delete zones in the Base Manager.
Zones persist across server restarts.
To re-do a selection, right-click again to restart from Corner 1.
topics.command: /bot zone wand, /bot zone list, /bot zone protect <radius> [label]
topics.tags: zone protect wand area region boundary admin

topics.title: Bot Enchanting
topics.summary: Enchant your companion's items using the bot's XP and lapis.
topics.answer: Stand near an enchanting table, open the Spells menu and click Enchant. You put my items and lapis in the table, and it uses my XP, not yours.
details: Open the Spells menu while near an Enchanting Table.
Click 'Enchant' to open the vanilla enchanting UI for your bot.
The inventory grid shows the bot's items. Drag items and lapis into the enchanting slots.
Enchantment offers are based on the bot's XP level, not yours.
XP and lapis are deducted from the bot. You keep your own levels.
Bookshelves around the table affect enchantment quality as normal.
When you close the screen, leftover items return to the bot's inventory.
Tip: bots accumulate XP from mining, combat, and fishing. Check their level in the inventory stats area.
topics.shortcuts: Stand near an Enchanting Table with bookshelves for best results
topics.tags: enchant enchanting table xp level lapis bot companion spells magic

topics.title: Bot Anvil
topics.summary: Repair, rename, or combine your companion's items using the bot's XP.
topics.answer: Stand near an anvil, open the Spells menu and click Anvil. You can repair, rename or combine my items, and the XP comes from me, not you.
details: Open the Spells menu while near an Anvil.
Click 'Anvil' to open the vanilla anvil UI for your bot.
The inventory grid shows the bot's items. Place items in the input slots as normal.
Repair: combine a damaged tool with its repair material or another copy.
Enchant: combine an item with an Enchanted Book to add enchantments.
Rename: type a new name in the text field (costs 1 level).
XP cost is deducted from the bot, not you.
Operations costing 40+ levels are blocked (vanilla 'Too Expensive' limit).
When you close the screen, leftover items return to the bot's inventory.
topics.tags: anvil repair rename combine enchanted book xp bot companion spells
